newsitem.title: ISRAEL: U.S. envoy upbeat after meeting Arafat on Hebron.
newsitem.headline: U.S. envoy upbeat after meeting Arafat on Hebron.

text.p: A U.S. Middle East envoy said on Monday he was upbeat about closing a deal soon on an Israeli army handover to Palestinians of part of the West Bank town of Hebron.

"I remain hopeful we will see an agreement soon but I can't predict when," U.S. envoy Dennis Ross told reporters after meeting Palestinian President Yasser Arafat in an office at the Church of the Nativity, the traditional birthplace of Jesus, in Palestinian-ruled Bethlehem.
"Both sides are making a real effort," Ross added.

Ross conducted intense negotiations on Monday, shuttling back and forth between Bethlehem and Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's Jerusalem office. By Monday night Ross was meeting Arafat for the second time in the day and was due to go back to Netanyahu's office later.

"Dennis Ross will arrive tonight at 10:30 p.m. (2030 gmt) to a meeting with the prime minister at the prime minister's office after meeting Arafat in Bethlehem," Netanyahu's spokesman said in a statement to reporters.

Israeli and Palestinian officials both said there could be an Arafat-Netanyahu summit later although none was scheduled. Palestinians said a summit to clinch a deal could take place in Beit Sahour outside Bethlehem.

Officials on both sides said earlier they had agreed on increasing the number of international observers to be posted in the volatile town after the Israeli redeployment. But the sides said they still had to sign that deal.

Palestinian negotiator Saeb Erekat said he and Israeli officials, meeting in Jericho, agreed to increase the number of observers in Hebron to 210 from 30 once Israel hands over 80 percent of the town to Palestinian self-rule.
"We reached agreement basically on all the points and now the agreements go to those in charge on each side. It's hard to estimate when it will be signed," an Israeli foreign ministry spokesman said.
Hebron, burial place of the biblical Abraham and home to 100,000 Palestinians and 400 Jewish settlers, has been a flashpoint of Jewish-Arab violence.

Security issues and other concerns over the last 10 months have delayed the Israeli handover to Arafat's PLO. Sources on both sides said remaining differences were over the dates of Israel's further handovers of West Bank land to the Palestinians.

"We have made a lot of progress. There is not a lot that separates the parties but there is not an agreement yet and we don't have an agreement until everything is resolved. And everything is not resolved," Ross said after meeting Netanyahu.

But a Palestinian official accused him of bias. Israel's newspaper Haaretz had quoted Ross and other U.S. officials as saying Netanyahu, stretched "to the outer limits of his flexibility," could concede no more.

"I am astonished by Dennis Ross's statements which expressed his completely biased disposition," Arafat's aide Marwan Kanafani told Israel Radio's Arabic service. "I think these statements harm the peace process."

Israel meanwhile eased its closure on the occupied territories, issuing permits to 50 more members of the Palestinian Authority to travel from the Gaza Strip to the West Bank, in addition to 150 who already hold permits.
